messages:
ali: quick pulse check — ran a small probe comparing Triton vs CUTLASS routing on H100 with seqlen slices (8/32/128). results look...biased towards triton at seqlen 8 but CUTLASS wins 32+ for batch=4. putting raw logs below, can folks eyeball? :thinking:

marie: nice, can you paste the kernel selection decision trace? especially want to see the probe plan and chosen kernels per layer.

ali: pasted. note the autotuner had a cold cache; probe config: `--probe-samples=50 --seed=42 --probe-seqlens="8,32,128" --batch=4`

ali: ```
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] probe: seq=8 sample=50 route=triton chosen_kernel=gemm_fused_triton_sm90 latency_ms=1.8
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] probe: seq=32 sample=50 route=cutlass chosen_kernel=cutlass_fp8_gemm latency_ms=2.6
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] probe: seq=128 sample=50 route=cutlass chosen_kernel=cutlass_split_kv latency_ms=5.1
[2026-03-15T15:12:04Z] fallback: seq=8 observed_kv_hit=0.12 routed_to=cutlass fallback_latency_ms=2.0
[2026-03-15T15:12:05Z] decision: runtime_prefers=triton if seqlen<=16 and p50_latency<=2.2ms
```

samir: interesting — fallback shows CUTLASS getting triton traffic for seq=8 on some paths. is that because of KV cache affinity heuristics?

ali: yes, the probe revealed a KV-affinity rule: if kv_hit_rate<0.2 we bias towards cutlass to avoid triton's small-batch inefficiency. but our recent autotune change tightened the latency threshold from 2.5->2.2ms which flips a bunch of seq=8 samples to triton.

dena: do we have perf counters for p99 tail? avg numbers are helpful but tail hurts production.

ali: added tail numbers from the same run:
```
seq=8: triton p50=1.8 p95=3.6 p99=9.8
seq=8: cutlass p50=2.0 p95=2.8 p99=3.5
seq=32: triton p50=3.5 p95=5.9 p99=9.9
seq=32: cutlass p50=2.6 p95=4.2 p99=6.0
```

marie: aha — at seqlen 8 triton wins on median but tail is terrible (p99 9.8ms). that explains why KV-affinity fallback occasionally prefers cutlass.

samir: is that tail coming from context-switches or batch-smearing under concurrent workloads? what's the concurrency in the probe?

ali: probe concurrency was 6 workers to simulate service load. digging into traces shows sporadic stalls during KV cache misses when triton kernel triggers re-compilation path for small batch combos. stack snippet below:
```
# simplified trace
KVLookup -> miss -> kernel_swap -> triton_autotune -> wait_compilation -> resume -> emit
```

dena: ugh autotune-triggered compilation at runtime. we should never compile on the hot path. suggest we add a guard: if compilation_time_estimate > 200ms then route to CUTLASS.

ali: agreed. currently we do heuristics but compilation estimates are missing for a few kernels. will add estimate table from offline profiler.

ops-bot: deploy-plan created by ali: patch/autotune-guard-compile-threshold -> staging queue (link: https://deploys.redwood/internal/1234) :white_check_mark:

marie: also consider adjusting KV-affinity threshold — if kv_hit_rate>0.15 prefer triton, else cutlass. the current 0.2 is too conservative given these tail numbers.

samir: quick sim: if we lower kv threshold to 0.12 we keep 70% of seq=8 on triton and tails still dominated by the 30% routed to cutlass — seems to give best cost/latency tradeoff. i'll run cost model later.

ali: thanks. action items: (1) ali add compilation-time estimates to kernel registry (PR incoming), (2) marie update KV-affinity to 0.12 and wire a canary, (3) samir run cost sim for commit tomorrow, (4) dena add p99 alert for kernel-compile stalls.

dena: can somebody add a small note in the runtime docs about "no-on-path-compilation" policy? we should make it explicit.

ali: will do. putting short doc snippet here: 
```
Runtime policy: avoid on-path kernel compilation for production traffic. If a kernel is not precompiled, route to the compatible alternative kernel variant (CUTLASS/Triton) with lower expected tail. Compilation should be gated to background warmers or canary traffic.
```

marie: good. ping me when the staging patch is up, i'll run the synthetic workload. :+1:

samir: will check cost sims by EOD.

ops-bot: staging deploy for patch/autotune-guard-compile-threshold succeeded: https://deploys.redwood/internal/1234/green :rocket:

ali: thanks team — keeping an eye on the canary, will report back with updated perf tables. :fire:
